column1: # Pull.fm - upstream egress classification for DAST scoping
# CANONICAL SOURCE, read by security/zap/scripts/scope-upstream.mjs.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS, SEPARATELY FROM x-pullfm-dast
# `x-pullfm-dast: include | exclude` answers ONE question: "would the scanner
# destroy the subject it is testing?" That is why DELETE /v1/me is excluded and
# GET /v1/artists/{mbid}/similar is included.
# It does not answer the question that can end this project. MusicBrainz permits
# 1 request per second GLOBALLY per IP and revokes without appeal
# (docs/UPSTREAM-TERMS.md, docs/PLAN.md section 8). A DAST crawler sends garbage
# identifiers by construction, every one of which is a guaranteed cache MISS, so
# "not destructive" and "will not egress to a provider" are different properties
# and the annotation only carried the first.
# Three operations annotated `x-pullfm-dast: include` can egress to a provider
# on scanner-shaped input. They are marked `egress` below and removed from the
# scanned spec. Relying on the DAST annotation alone would have scanned them.
# CLASSIFICATIONS
#   none           A request to this operation cannot cause an outbound HTTP
#                  call to a third-party provider, on any input, hit or miss.
#                  Scanned.
#   subject-gated  Can egress, but only when the AUTHENTICATED SUBJECT holds a
#                  stored provider credential. Scanned only when the runner has
#                  PROVED the scan subject holds zero connections
#                  (`connectionCount == 0` on GET /v1/me) and passed
#                  --allow-subject-gated. Excluded by default.
#   egress         Can cause an outbound provider call on input a scanner will
#                  actually send. NEVER scanned. There is no flag to include
#                  these; removing the flag is the control.
# The `providers` column names who is reached, so a future reader can re-derive
# the decision rather than trust it.
# FAILS CLOSED. scope-upstream.mjs reconciles this register against the spec in
# BOTH directions: an operation in the spec with no row here is a hard failure,
# and a row here with no operation in the spec is a hard failure. A new route
# therefore cannot be scanned until somebody has answered the egress question in
# writing. That is the same shape as the prune-openapi.mjs refusal to default an
# unannotated operation, and for the same reason: the convenient default is the
# one that gets our provider access revoked.
# THE STRONGER FIX, RECOMMENDED. This belongs on the route as a required field
# of `PullfmAnnotations` (apps/bff/src/lib/openapi.ts) next to `dast`, so the
# classification is written where the fetch is written and cannot be forgotten
# in a second file. It is here instead because that is 38 route-definition edits
# across six files in a tree other agents are writing to, and the reconciliation
# below gives the same fail-closed property today. See security/DAST-RUNBOOK.md.
# TAB-SEPARATED, like security/zap/rules/baseline-rules.tsv. Format:
#   <METHOD> <path><TAB><classification><TAB><providers><TAB><evidence>
# Blank lines and lines beginning with # are ignored.
# --- Platform surface. No provider client is reachable from any of these. -----
GET /healthz
column4: Postgres and Redis liveness only; no upstream client is constructed on this path.

column1: GET /readyz
column4: Postgres and Redis readiness only.

column1: GET /metrics
column4: Reads the local prom-client registry. Also gated to loopback or METRICS_TOKEN (routes/health.ts) and denied at nginx.

column1: GET /v1/config
column4: Reads the in-memory provider status snapshot (services/upstream.ts status()); does not refresh it.

column1: # --- Auth. WorkOS is our identity provider, not a rate-limited music provider.
# It is not in docs/UPSTREAM-TERMS.md and has no per-IP request ceiling we can
# breach. Every one of these is `x-pullfm-dast: exclude` anyway, so none reaches
# the scanner; classified here only because the register must be total.
POST /v1/auth/start
column4: Calls WorkOS magic-auth. Not a metered music provider. Already dast:exclude. The call is now additionally gated by the EEA/UK/CH registration refusal (lib/registration-geo.ts), which runs at onRequest, so a refused region produces zero egress rather than a created directory record.

column1: POST /v1/auth/verify
column4: As above, and behind the same registration-region gate.

column1: GET /v1/auth/callback
column4: As above, and behind the same registration-region gate.

column1: POST /v1/auth/refresh
column4: As above.

column1: POST /v1/auth/logout
column4: As above.

column1: GET /v1/me
column4: Reads users and counts; no provider client on the path.

column1: DELETE /v1/me
column4: Deletion cascade calls WorkOS deleteUser. Already dast:exclude for destructiveness.

column1: PATCH /v1/me
column4: WorkOS updateUser. Already dast:exclude.

column1: GET /v1/me/export
column4: Local export job. Already dast:exclude and in the ZAP context excludePaths.

column1: GET /v1/me/export/download
column4: Serves a local artefact. Already dast:exclude.

column1: GET /v1/me/consent
column4: Reads legal_document_revisions and legal_consents plus an in-memory document registry. No provider client exists on this path and no input can put one there.

column1: POST /v1/me/consent
column4: Inserts a consent row after comparing the supplied version and content digest to the registry. No provider client on the path; dast:exclude anyway, because a scanner cannot produce a valid digest and so could only exercise the refusal branches, while a fuzzer that DID get through would be writing rows into the table whose value is that every row corresponds to a real human act.

column1: # --- Personal API tokens. Entirely local. -------------------------------------
GET /v1/tokens
column4: Postgres only.

column1: POST /v1/tokens
column4: Postgres only. dast:exclude because it mints credentials.

column1: DELETE /v1/tokens/{id}
column4: Postgres only.

column1: POST /v1/tokens/{id}/rotate
column4: Postgres only.

column1: # --- Connections. Two of these egress, and one does so on EVERY request. ------
GET /v1/connections
column4: Postgres only; does not validate stored credentials against the provider.

column1: POST /v1/connections/{service}
column4: services/providers.ts validate-token: one UNCACHED call to api.listenbrainz.org per request carrying a token body field. No cache, no gate. Already dast:exclude, but for credential reasons, not this one.

column1: DELETE /v1/connections/{service}
column4: Local revoke; does not notify the provider.

column1: GET /v1/connections/{service}/callback
column4: services/providers.ts auth.getSession against ws.audioscrobbler.com. Guarded by a signed single-use state, so a scanner is rejected first, but the guard is one bug away from being the only thing between a fuzzer and Last.fm. Also excluded at the ZAP context level.

column1: # --- Wishlist. Acquisition links are built as strings, not resolved. ----------
GET /v1/wishlist
column4: Postgres only.

column1: POST /v1/wishlist
column4: Postgres only.

column1: DELETE /v1/wishlist/{id}
column4: Postgres only.

column1: GET /v1/wishlist/{id}/acquire
column4: services/wishlist.ts constructs vendor URLs by string interpolation. No outbound call.

column1: # --- Personalised discovery. Gated on the SUBJECT holding a credential. -------
# Every one of these opens the caller's stored ListenBrainz credential first and
# returns a degraded section when there is none, so a subject with zero
# connections cannot make them egress. The runner proves that rather than
# assuming it.
GET /v1/feed
column4: discovery.ts openCredential returns null for a subject with no connection and every port short-circuits before the client is called.

column1: GET /v1/recommendations
column4: Same credential gate as /v1/feed.

column1: GET /v1/stations
column4: ListenBrainz topArtists behind the same gate, cached per user per month.

column1: GET /v1/stations/{id}/tracks
column4: ListenBrainz artistRadio. Additionally HMAC-gated: a forged station id is rejected before any port is touched.

column1: # --- Catalogue. This is where the DAST annotation was not enough. -------------
# MusicBrainz is NOT reachable from any of these. Every request-path MusicBrainz
# read goes through CachedUpstream.peek, which is database-only and returns null
# on a miss rather than calling load(). The MusicBrainz client is reached only by
# the background cache-warmer job (services/cache-warmer.ts) and the offline
# warm-cache script. That is why the pacer cannot move during a scan, and it is
# a property of the code rather than of the scan configuration.
GET /v1/search
column4: crosswalkStore.search is a Postgres trigram query. No provider call on hit or miss.

column1: GET /v1/artists/{mbid}
column4: peek + crosswalk, database-only. An unknown mbid returns 404 without egress.

column1: GET /v1/artists/{mbid}/similar
column4: THE DANGEROUS ONE. #labsSimilarArtists calls labs.api.listenbrainz.org for ANY well-formed UUID with no prior existence check, and a random UUID is a guaranteed cache miss, so a scanner gets one outbound call per request. Annotated dast:include, which is why the DAST annotation alone was not a sufficient control.

column1: GET /v1/tracks/{mbid}
column4: peek only, database-only.

column1: GET /v1/tracks/{mbid}/preview
column4: Deezer resolution on the request path, deliberately never cached because the signed URLs expire. A warm recording is required first, so a garbage mbid does not egress today; excluded anyway because that safety is an accident of the cache state, not a control.

column1: GET /v1/albums/{mbid}
column4: peek only, database-only.

column1: GET /v1/artists/{mbid}/events
column4: SeatGeek events. Requires a warm artist, but the cache key includes city/state/country, so fuzzing the geo query parameters against ONE valid artist produces one SeatGeek call per distinct combination. Annotated dast:include.

column1: POST /v1/webhooks/workos
column4: Verifies a signature and writes locally.
